method: HMTc government-limit-only initial standard; exact sovereign maximum, then disclosed sovereign read-across, then explicit control/no-numeric determination

categories.name: Infant and Child Foods
categories.note: Formula powder and ready-to-feed rows each retain cow/non-soy and soy variants.

categories.name: Seafood
categories.note: Includes the six locked seafood rows plus the separately compiled cephalopod row.

categories.name: Oils, Condiments, and Specialty Foods
categories.note: Eight scope-locked rows compile. Four broad rows remain blocked on the taxonomy/product-basis splits recorded in the Step-0 lock.

categories.name: Dietary Supplements (Human)
categories.note: Child-protective over-compliance: every subcategory is set to the strictest sovereign infant-and-child-food maximum level (Ages 0-5) and held to it regardless of adult/child labeling. Cr, Cr-VI, and MeHg are mandatory controls (no infant-food total-Cr ML; Cr-VI reduces to Cr-III; MeHg bounded by tHg with lot speciation on marine-source classes). The adult floor (supplement ML / USP <2232> / Prop 65 MADL) is disclosed on every cell and never selects the number.

categories.name: Cannabis, Hemp, and CBD Products
categories.note: Five route-defined material/product rows compile. Vape hardware remains blocked on the lock's reserved aerosol-release/shared-hardware architecture decision.

policy_blocked_categories.name: Peptides, SARMs, and Research Chemicals
policy_blocked_categories.reason: No lawful product-specific sovereign maximum exists, and the parenteral/oral dose-basis method is not yet governed. Occurrence or a health-based calculation cannot replace the missing government anchor under the current initial-limit rule.
